but is not resolved by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/86808  
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/72491 doesn't look like it would resolve this specific crash either

In my Project I'm extensively using Shape Cast 3Ds with 4.5 beta 4 standard with jolt on a separate thread, even with Physics Interpolation without issues. I haven't tested beta 5 yet

Edit - in 4.5 Beta 5 now and I still Haven't been able to recreate this issue in My Project.
Does this happen in 4.4.1? Or is it a regression?

It would seem that this is pretty bad, and quite the fundamental flaw in how `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` works (or rather doesn't work) together with `PhysicsDirectSpaceState*D`. I'm not sure how it's taken this long for this problem to surface, nor how I have somehow misunderstood this so thoroughly myself, unless there's some recent change to all this that I'm missing. Basically, when you enable the `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` project setting, the physics server in Godot gets wrapped in a `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT`. This essentially adds a giant thread-synchronized command queue around it, which ensures that only the dedicated physics thread reads/writes from/to the physics server. So any mutating operation (i.e. setter) will be queued up and flushed from the physics thread at some later point, and any read (i.e. getter) will block until the command queue is done with any ongoing operation. However, there are some exceptions to this, namely `PhysicsDirectSpaceState*D` and `PhysicsDirectBodyState*D`, which as the names suggest provide you with direct access to the "space" (e.g. `intersect_ray`) and the body without going through the physics server or its command queue wrapper. For whatever reason I was convinced that the command queue in `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT` was blocked for the part of the main loop ([this chunk of code](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/main/main.cpp#L4738-L4777)) where the user/developer would reasonably perform physics operations, meaning `_integrate_forces`, `_physics_process` and contact/area signal emissions. When that's the case then the only thing that could reasonably happen in parallel would be calls to `PhysicsDirectSpaceState*D` and `PhysicsDirectBodyState*D`, which all rightfully should be read-only operations and thus thread-safe. However, this is simply not the case. `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT` will happily chug along and flush potentially mutating commands while the user is performing physics queries in something like `_physics_process`, which is obviously a blatant race condition unless accounted for, which it isn't. The race condition that's being triggered in this particular repro seems to be that [Terrain3D](https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D) tries to change the shape data of one of its `HeightMapShape3D`, presumably due to LODing or chunking, which means that we're mutating shapes on the physics thread (as part of flushing the commands) while querying against them on the main thread (as part of calling `cast_motion` from `ShapeCast3D`) which is very bad. This also means that this problem is not exclusive to Jolt, and affects both the 2D and 3D versions of Godot Physics as well. To verify this I fired up [this simple MRP](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21756765/physics-race-condition.zip) in a build with ThreadSanitizer (using `use_tsan=yes`) and suppressed whatever issues we currently have with ThreadSanitizer until I finally arrived at this:

The tl;dr of that would be that we are changing the size of a `BoxShape3D` from the physics thread while we're reading said size from a `ShapeCast3D` on the main thread, which is very bad. So assuming there hasn't been some recent functional change to either `PhysicsServer3DWrapMT`, `CommandQueueMT` or the main loop, then this has likely been an issue for a long time and likely caused a number of weird problems. It just so happens that it manifested as a crash in this particular repro. --- I'm honestly not sure what the best fix for this might be. My kneejerk reaction would be to change it so that the physics thread command queue is in fact blocked[^1] between `PhysicsServer*D::sync` and `PhysicsServer*D::end_sync`, but I'm not totally sure of the ramifications of such a change. [^1]: Calling a getter on the physics server would presumably need to just directly call the function in that case.

> The tl;dr of that would be that we are changing the size of a `BoxShape3D` from the physics thread while we're reading said size from a `ShapeCast3D` on the main thread, which is very bad.

I can confirm that this race condition happens with `GodotPhysics3D` in 4.4.1-stable and 4.3-stable as well, so it's not a recent regression at least, if at all.

What's really throwing me off is [the documentation](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/doc/classes/ProjectSettings.xml#L2526) for `run_on_separate_thread` seemingly reinforcing my previous understanding of it:

> Running the physics server on a separate thread can increase performance, but restricts API access to only physics process.

But the only applicable restriction in this case is that you can't call `PhysicsServer*D.space_get_direct_state` or `PhysicsServer*D.body_get_direct_state` outside of the physics processing methods when `run_on_separate_thread` is enabled:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_physics_server_3d.cpp#L194

... which would seem to suggest that they were intended to be safely accessed within the physics processing methods when we're `doing_sync`, but clearly they're not.

Well, I decided to give this a try, and it does technically resolve the issue, but likely at a non-trivial performance cost: #109591

This might be the issue that made my web exports to not detect physics collisions. Rigid bodies went through static bodies & area3ds didn't detect any characterbody3ds on the web exports without ThreadingSupport enabled. This was on 4.5_beta6. I had tried to look for answers but updating now to 4.5_rc1 fixes my issue.
Looking into the changelog & saw this issue, I thought it was kind of similar and I had to report something that might be useful in future because I didn't see it brought up anywhere else online

I don't think that's related to this issue, nor the fix in #109591. I suspect you ran into the regression that came from #108768 in 4.5-beta6, which was later reverted in #110003 for 4.5-beta7.
